name: Dark Peach
lede: Dark Peach is a deep, reddish version of [[peach]], closer to terracotta than to the pale fruit tone most people picture.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No Western book in our library records a name at this exact position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark peach" [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the nearest block as a moderate reddish orange, about 6 CIEDE2000 units away, with a Munsell reading near 0.1YR in hue [1].

Our library's cross-reference to Japanese traditional color names pairs this position with *tokigaracha* (ときがら茶), glossed as "brewed mustard-brown": that is an approximate color match across two naming systems, not a claim that the Japanese name and "dark peach" share a history [1]. Its nearest English neighbors in our library are [[peach]], [[terracotta]] and [[camel]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 50 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. A Dutch portrait of a puppy from 1850 carries the most of it, covering 42 per cent of the canvas, and Amedeo Modigliani's paintings carry it 79 times the archive's baseline rate [2]. It is also common in Rajput, Kalighat and Mughal miniature painting, and the word "Terracotta" shares its canvases far more than chance [2]. Where it appears, it splits fairly evenly between a mid-tone and a highlight [2].
